pr_title: daemon: fix under what conditions container's mac-address is applied
pr_body:
**- What I did**

- Fix https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/46404
- Fix docker/compose#10796

The daemon would pass an EndpointCreateOption to set the interface MAC address if the network name and the provided network mode were matching. Obviously, if the network mode is a network ID, it won't work. To make things worse, the network mode is never normalized if it's a partial ID.

To fix that: 1. the condition under what the container's mac-address is applied is updated to also match the full ID; 2. the network mode is normalized to a full ID when it's only a partial one.

**- How to verify it**

```
$ docker run --rm --name test --network 6cabee8406 --mac-address "02:42:ac:11:00:02" nicolaka/netshoot ip -brief link show dev eth0
eth0@if92        UP             02:42:ac:11:00:02 <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> 
```

**- A picture of a cute animal (not mandatory but encouraged)**

![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/d4/Sea_otter_pair2.jpg)

issue_context.title: --mac-address not respected when targeting network by ID
issue_context.body:
### Description

`docker run` doesn't respect `--mac-address` flag when used with a macvlan network identified by ID, while it works as expected when using name

### Reproduce

1. docker network create --driver macvlan --subnet "192.168.100.0/24" --gateway "192.168.100.1" foobar
2. docker run --network <network ID> --mac-address "02:42:ac:11:00:02" --ip "192.168.100.103" -d nginx
3. docker inspect <container> | jq '.[] | .NetworkSettings.Networks | any | .MacAddress'




### Expected behavior

`02:42:ac:11:00:02` as requested by `--mac-address`, or some error if there's a technical reason this isn't possible to assign

doing the same but using `--network <network NAME>` the requested mac address is assigned as expected.

comments:
As I'm digging a bit, I found that this also happen with the `bridge` netdriver.

Libnetwork stores network settings twice (once keyed by network name as expected, and once more keyed by network ID) when both `--network <nid>` and `--ip` are specified together:

```console
$ docker network create --subnet 192.168.100.0/24 testnet
6cabee8406b06309583cd90e1a30d6dc05438b781c7d649d3334cd326b32dd3d

$ docker run --rm --network testnet --mac-address "02:42:ac:11:00:02" --ip "192.168.100.103" nicolaka/netshoot /bin/bash -c "ip -brief link show eth0 && ip -brief addr show eth0"
eth0@if39        UP             02:42:ac:11:00:02 <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> 
eth0@if39        UP             192.168.100.103/24 

$ docker run --rm --network 6cabee8406 --mac-address "02:42:ac:11:00:02" --ip "192.168.100.103" nicolaka/netshoot /bin/bash -c "ip -brief link show eth0 && ip -brief addr show eth0"
eth0@if41        UP             02:42:c0:a8:64:67 <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> 
eth0@if41        UP             192.168.100.103/24 

$ docker run --rm --name test --network testnet --mac-address "02:42:ac:11:00:02" --ip "192.168.100.103" -d nginx >/dev/null; docker inspect test | jq '.[] | .NetworkSettings.Networks[] | .IPAddress, .MacAddress'; docker rm --force test >/dev/null
"192.168.100.103"
"02:42:ac:11:00:02"

$ docker run --rm --name test --network 6cabee8406 --mac-address "02:42:ac:11:00:02" --ip "192.168.100.103" -d nginx >/dev/null; docker inspect test | jq '.[] | .NetworkSettings.Networks[] | .IPAddress, .MacAddress'; docker rm --force test >/dev/null
"192.168.100.103"
"02:42:c0:a8:64:67"
"192.168.100.103"
"02:42:c0:a8:64:67"

$ docker run --rm --name test --network 6cabee8406 --ip "192.168.100.103" -d nginx >/dev/null; docker inspect test | jq '.[] | .NetworkSettings.Networks | keys'; docker rm --force test >/dev/null
[
  "6cabee8406",
  "testnet"
]

$ docker run --rm --name test --network 6cabee8406 -d nginx >/dev/null; docker inspect test | jq '.[] | .NetworkSettings.Networks | keys'; docker rm --force test >/dev/null
[
  "testnet"
]

$ docker run --rm --name test --network 6cabee8406 --mac-address "02:42:ac:11:00:02" -d nginx >/dev/null; docker inspect test | jq '.[] | .NetworkSettings.Networks | keys'; docker rm --force test >/dev/null
[
  "testnet"
]
```

However, that seems unrelated to the bug reported by @ndeloof as the MAC address is still wrong when no `--ip` flag is not specified:

```console
$ docker run --rm --name test --network 6cabee8406 --mac-address "02:42:ac:11:00:02" nicolaka/netshoot ip -brief link show dev eth0
eth0@if68        UP             02:42:c0:a8:64:02 <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> 

$ docker run --rm --name test --network testnet --mac-address "02:42:ac:11:00:02" nicolaka/netshoot ip -brief link show dev eth0
eth0@if70        UP             02:42:ac:11:00:02 <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP>
```

review_comments:
I really don't like the idea of mutating the network mode in `connectToNetwork` but there's no other choice: if the network mode references a swarm-scope network, it might not exist on the local node before `findAndAttachNetwork` is executed. As a Swarm agent doesn't have access to the list of swarm-scope networks, this is the only place where `normalizeNetMode` can be called.

As discussed with @thaJeztah today, I think it'd be preferable to create uninitialized/placeholder swarm-scope networks on every node. That would make the UX better and it'd restore the original semantics (ie. a container can't connect to a network that don't exist locally). That would make the code easier to reason about, we'd be able to move the call to `normalizeNetMode` upper in the call stack, and we'd not need to create a Swarm task in `findAndAttachNetwork` (ie. this too could be moved upper in the stack).
This should be done in a follow-up PR.
